name: EuroSAT
description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images for land use and land cover classification, consisting of 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches across 10 classes and covering 13 spectral bands.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. Introducing EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. 2018 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS), 2018.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in two steps: (1) satellite image acquisition and (2) dataset creation. The authors downloaded Sentinel-2A satellite images via Amazon S3, choosing images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas and distributed over 34 European countries. They selected images with low cloud level and extracted images recorded all over the year to increase variance. Based on the obtained satellite images, they created 27,000 geo-referenced and labeled image patches of size 64x64 pixels, which were manually checked.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of multi-spectral Sentinel-2A satellite images downloaded via Amazon S3, associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Image patches of size 64x64 pixels were extracted from Sentinel-2A satellite images. The dataset includes RGB and multi-spectral versions. For band evaluation, bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors selected satellite images with low cloud level to improve the chance of getting valuable image patches. They manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. The dataset did not receive atmospheric correction, so images with color cast due to atmospheric effects were retained.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of labeled image patches created based on 10 land use and land cover classes chosen because they are visible at 10 meters per pixel and frequently covered by the European Urban Atlas. The composition of the individual classes and their relationships are specified in the mapping guide of the European Urban Atlas. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually checked all images multiple times and corrected ground truth by removing mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice. They note that the classifier sometimes confuses the agricultural land classes as well as the classes highway and river.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Georeferenced image locations distributed over 34 European countries.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the dataset and resulting classification system open the way to Earth observation applications such as agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, environmental monitoring, land use and land cover change detection, deforestation detection, and assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. The authors selected images associated with European cities, selected images with low cloud level, and aimed to cover as many countries as possible and images recorded all over the year to capture high intra-class variance. They also note low positive correlation between some classes, especially the two agricultural classes and the residential and industrial building classes.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset uses 10 meter per pixel Sentinel-2 imagery, so classes were chosen based on visibility at that resolution. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes and the classes highway and river. The patch-based classification system trained on 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark and training basis for supervised land use and land cover classification using deep neural networks. The paper uses training-test splits for benchmarking, including an 80/20 split and other ratios. It is also proposed for real-world Earth observation applications such as land use and land cover change detection and assistance in improving and updating geographical maps.
